D161.call_notes:
Rep: Thanks for jumping back on, Soren. Maren, good to meet you. Where do things stand on your end?

Rep: Then is there room to put our proposal next to hers?
Soren Nakamura (Chief People Officer): I don't think so. I'd be going against our broker. I don't want to do that. She's been right too many times.

Soren Nakamura (Chief People Officer): Of course. You were a good conversation. Just not the one she brought us.

Soren Nakamura (Chief People Officer): Fair. Keep my number.

D162.call_notes:
Rep: Jules! Good to catch you. How's the week going?
Jules Vasquez (Chief People Officer): Oh, you know, one of those weeks. A press went down on Monday, so everyone's been running around the floor, and I've barely looked at email. Sorry for the slow reply, by the way.

Jules Vasquez (Chief People Officer): Right, right. So, okay. Funny story, except it's not funny. Our CEO, who was the one pushing this whole thing, he's stepping away at the end of the quarter. Family stuff, health stuff, I don't want to get into it. And the board basically said nobody starts anything big until the new person is in the chair.
Ravi Tillbrook (Head of People): Which means we're frozen. Not just us. Everything with a spend attached.
Jules Vasquez (Chief People Officer): Yeah. We were really close, Ravi will tell you. We loved the demo, the walk-through of the payroll runs was exactly what I was hoping for. And the price was, I mean, it was fine, it was in the range we'd talked about.
Ravi Tillbrook (Head of People): Nobody here is saying no to you. It's just not a yes to anybody right now. We're still on the old spreadsheets and the old provider contract.
Rep: So no other vendor in the picture?
Jules Vasquez (Chief People Officer): No, no, nobody. We just stopped. Maybe spring, maybe later, honestly I can't tell you. Can I ping you when things unfreeze?

Jules Vasquez (Chief People Officer): Will do. And tell your team thanks again, they were great. Anyway, I should go, someone's yelling about a pallet.

D163.call_notes:
Teodoro Parekh (HR Director): Thank you for making time again. I wanted to give you our decision in person, rather than by email.
Rep: I appreciate that. Where did you land?
Teodoro Parekh (HR Director): We will be going with Tallyhold. I should say it was not an easy conclusion, and nothing in your demonstration was poor.
Rep: Can you tell me what it came down to?
Teodoro Parekh (HR Director): Primarily our broker. Our broker has handled our benefits renewals for, I believe, nine years. When she brought us the bundle, payroll, benefits administration and time tracking together, she presented it as the recommended path. We trust her judgement, and we are following it.
Signe Castellane (COO): If I may. We did not run a full comparison against your proposal. The bundle was what the broker put in front of us, and in our experience she has never steered us wrong. She also negotiates the carrier rates, so keeping that relationship sound matters to us.
Rep: Understood. Was there anything about our platform that gave you pause?
Teodoro Parekh (HR Director): One small matter, and I mention it only for completeness. We have staff in five states, and the time-off accrual rules differ by location. Your system, as I understood it, applies one accrual policy per company. That was noted. It was not what decided this.
Signe Castellane (COO): No. It was the broker.
Rep: I'm grateful for the candour.
Teodoro Parekh (HR Director): Of course. We would be glad to keep in touch should circumstances change at our next renewal.

D164.call_notes:
Rep: Ravi, Sunniva, thanks for hopping on.
Ravi Thorsen (COO): Quick news. We're signing with you.
Rep: That's great to hear. Can I ask what made the difference?
Ravi Thorsen (COO): Two things. The demo first. Most vendors show me a slideshow. You asked what our payroll week looks like. Then you built it live. Two states, one hourly crew, one salaried. That was our actual mess.
Sunniva Parekh (Compliance Lead): I had questions on audit trails. Your person didn't dodge. Pulled up the log, showed me who changed what and when. I liked that.
Ravi Thorsen (COO): Second thing. The rollout plan. Six weeks. Week by week. Names next to every task. Corvane gave us a PDF that said phase one, phase two. No dates.
Rep: Did the Corvane quote come close?
Ravi Thorsen (COO): Close enough. It wasn't the money. It was knowing what happens on day thirty.
Sunniva Parekh (Compliance Lead): One complaint, though. Your mobile app. It logs me out every time I switch to email and back. Every time. I've re-entered my password maybe ten times this week.
Rep: That's frustrating, and I'll pass it to the product team today.
Ravi Thorsen (COO): It's annoying. It's not a dealbreaker. We're not approving payroll on a phone.
Sunniva Parekh (Compliance Lead): Just fix it.
Rep: Noted. So, next steps. I'll send the paperwork this afternoon.
Ravi Thorsen (COO): Good. Send it to both of us. Kickoff the week of the eighteenth if that works.
Rep: It does.

D165.call_notes:
Bram Hartigan (Chief People Officer): So, I've been going back and forth on this, and I figured I owe you a straight answer. We're not going to move forward. And it's, hm, it's one thing really.
Rep: I'd appreciate knowing what it is.
Bram Hartigan (Chief People Officer): Approvals. Okay, so, here's how it works for us. A raise request, or a bonus, goes from the team lead to the department head, then it goes to Yuki for the budget check, then it comes back to me. Four stops, and the order matters. In the demo, you showed me one approver. Maybe two if I squint.
Yuki Santangelo (CFO): Right, and I asked about it twice. Chaining the steps, conditional on the dollar amount. Over five thousand, it adds a step. Your answer was it's on the roadmap.
Bram Hartigan (Chief People Officer): Which, fine, it might be, but we're not going to run raises over email in the meantime. That's the exact thing we're trying to leave behind. I keep thinking, could we live with it for six months? And honestly no, probably not.
Rep: Is there anything else outstanding on your side?
Bram Hartigan (Chief People Officer): No, no. Payroll looked good. Tax side looked good. Price was fine. It's really just the approvals thing.
Yuki Santangelo (CFO): Come back to us when that's built.

D166.call_notes:
Tobias Jessamy (Director of Operations): Okay so I wanted to call rather than email, because I feel like you earned a call. We're going to pass.

So every quarter our board wants, let me think, headcount by campus, overtime by campus, turnover, and then they always ask some new question I can't predict. Tobias Jessamy (Director of Operations): Right. I was hoping for something like, drag in the fields, slice it how you want. We never saw that. Did we? I might be forgetting.
Rep: The standard reports are fixed, yes. A custom report builder isn't available yet.
Tobias Jessamy (Director of Operations): Yeah. That's what I thought. And, to be fair, the payroll piece, great. Taxes in our five states, fine. Price, totally fine, I'm not even going to pretend price was it.
Mirela Jessamy (Head of Finance): Our board chair is particular. We can't go to her with fixed reports.
Tobias Jessamy (Director of Operations): So, yeah. Sorry. It's not you, it's the board packet.

D167.call_notes:

D167.closing_email:

D168.call_notes:
Ravi Quillfeather (People Operations Lead): Thanks for the revised proposal. I went through it with Mirela line by line, and I'll give you the numbers so there's no ambiguity.
Rep: Please.

Ravi Quillfeather (People Operations Lead): I did ask myself that. But phasing just moves the cost. Payroll by itself would still be around thirty a head, so we'd save, what, maybe eight dollars? Still above.

Ravi Quillfeather (People Operations Lead): Right. If your pricing moves next year, call me.

D169.call_notes:

Amara Galbraith (VP of People): It mattered. We had momentum. People were still excited. Second thing, the demo answered what we asked. Not a script. I asked about tracking PTO for our vets who work split shifts. You showed it. Live.

Jules Abernethy (Controller): I asked about pricing tiers. I asked what happens when we add the third clinic. I asked what the implementation fee covers and what it doesn't. You didn't hedge. You put it in writing the same afternoon.

Jules Abernethy (Controller): The fee for off-cycle checks. And the cost of the extra reporting seat. Fine. I can budget for those. What I can't budget for is surprises.

Jules Abernethy (Controller): We're comfortable. Honestly, more than I expected to be.

D170.call_notes:

Hi, Emeka from Redfern Freight. Wanted to follow up in writing. We've gone ahead with another provider. The eight days between our first call and the demo meant we'd already started elsewhere by the time we saw yours. Thanks for your time and for the thoughtful walkthrough.

Emeka

Ingrid Oyelaran (HR Generalist): I'll give you the decision first. We're not buying.

Ingrid Oyelaran (HR Generalist): Reporting. Specifically what our board wants.

Yuki Zeller (General Manager): Every quarter our investors want a labor cost view. Cost per hire by department. Against plan. Plus the mix of contractors versus employees. And it's never the same ask twice. Last quarter it was overtime as a share of payroll, by team lead. The quarter before, it was raises by tenure.
Ingrid Oyelaran (HR Generalist): I build those by hand today. Exports into spreadsheets. It takes me two days.

Yuki Zeller (General Manager): A report library. Good one. Maybe thirty reports. Fixed. You can filter, you can export. You can't build your own view.
Ingrid Oyelaran (HR Generalist): I asked three times. Can I add a field. Can I group by something else. Can I save it. The answer was no, no, not yet.
Yuki Zeller (General Manager): That's the whole point of this project. If I'm still exporting to a spreadsheet, nothing has changed.
Rep: Anything else?
Ingrid Oyelaran (HR Generalist): No. Payroll was clean. Taxes were fine. Price was fine. I want that on the record.
Yuki Zeller (General Manager): Reporting. That's the one.

Yuki Zeller (General Manager): If you build it, tell me. I'll look again.

Priya Okonkwo (HR Director): Hi there, sorry, I'm in the car, the Bluetooth is awful, can you hear me okay? Greta's on the other line.
Rep: Loud and clear.
Priya Okonkwo (HR Director): Great. So I wanted to circle back on our question list, the one from last week. I've been thinking about it all weekend, which is sad.
Rep: Let's go through it.
Priya Okonkwo (HR Director): Okay, so, we've got people in four states now, and one of the things that keeps me up is, I've got a technician who lives in Kentucky and works in our Ohio office. Does your system figure out that reciprocity thing, so she isn't getting Kentucky and Ohio both taken out? Because last time she had both and she was, rightly, furious.
Rep: In that case, I'd want to confirm with our tax team how the reciprocity certificate gets recorded.
Priya Okonkwo (HR Director): That's what you said last time. We'd have to check.
Greta Brannigan (Compliance Lead): And the other one. When somebody moves mid-year, say Indiana to Illinois in August, how does the withholding split? Who files the changes with the state? Are we on the hook?
Rep: Honestly, I don't have a clean answer there. We'd have to check with the compliance group.
Priya Okonkwo (HR Director): And I know it's silly, but those are the two things. If the tax part isn't airtight we can't, you know. Price, yes, I noticed it's a little higher than we figured, but that's not it. We'd pay it.
Greta Brannigan (Compliance Lead): We can't guess on this.
Priya Okonkwo (HR Director): So we're going with Corvane. They walked us through both examples on the call. I'll send you a note.
D173.closing_email:
Subject: Our decision

Hi,

Thank you again for all the time you and your team gave us. We've decided to go with Corvane. The deciding piece for Greta and me was how payroll taxes get handled across our four states, particularly the Kentucky and Ohio reciprocity situation and mid-year moves. We needed firm answers and, on those two, we didn't get them. The rest of what we saw was good, and the price was reasonable. We'd happily look again if that area develops.

Best,
Priya

Odalys Dunmore (HR Director): Let's get to it. I have a hard stop at three.

Rep: I believe we handle the filing at the state level. For the local collector, I'd have to check.
Hollis Zeller (Controller): That's what I heard. Second one. We're hiring our first person in Tennessee next month. Who registers us with the state for unemployment, and how fast?
Rep: We'd have to check on the timeline.
Odalys Dunmore (HR Director): Look, we don't need perfect. We need confident. If I can't tell my CEO who files what in a new state, I can't put payroll on this.
Hollis Zeller (Controller): Price is a little above where I thought. Whatever. I'd pay it.
Odalys Dunmore (HR Director): So that's it. Tax handling.
Rep: Understood. Thanks for being direct.
Odalys Dunmore (HR Director): Appreciate the time.

D175.call_notes:
Marisol Cadogan (COO): Good afternoon. Thank you both for joining. I will be candid, as I think you deserve that.

Marisol Cadogan (COO): We have not chosen Lanternmere HR. We operate in eight states, and the payroll tax question has not been resolved to our satisfaction. Wren, would you summarise?

Wren Zeller (Payroll Manager): Second, Colorado. The family leave insurance premiums are split between employer and employee, and the rate changes. I asked who updates the rate and who files the quarterly report. Again, the response was that you would have to check.
Marisol Cadogan (COO): I do not want to be unfair. The people we met were knowledgeable in other areas. The product demonstration was good. Pricing, if I may, is somewhat higher than we expected, but it is not what this is about. We would have paid it.

Marisol Cadogan (COO): A written description of how each of those is handled, state by state, would have changed it. We could not get to that point. And, in fairness, the project was already slowing down internally. Our finance director asked to delay anything non-essential until the new year. So the timing was not ideal either.
Wren Zeller (Payroll Manager): But the tax handling, mainly.
Marisol Cadogan (COO): Yes. That is the main matter.
Rep: Thank you. I'll pass that to our product team.
Marisol Cadogan (COO): Please do. We wish you well.
D175.closing_email:

Marisol, thank you for the candid feedback. I've shared the Oregon transit tax and Colorado premium questions with our payroll tax team, and I'll send written answers when they're ready, in case it's useful later. Wishing you and Wren the best.
